{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 119,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Guard the missing destination calendar in the Google Meet fallback",
      "body": "When destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. A booking with Google Meet selected then throws while reading .integration, instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. This can happen after disconnecting Google Calendar while retaining a Google Meet event location. Use an optional access or explicitly handle the missing destination."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 370,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Select the current host's destination before invoking calendar adapters",
      "body": "Every credential receives the complete destinationCalendar array, but Office365, Lark, and CalDAV still select its first entry. Consequently, a second Outlook host attempts to create an event in the first host's calendar using the second host's credentials; CalDAV can filter out every calendar and silently report success without creating anything. Google's organizer attendee also uses the first externalId, which is not a valid email when the main destination is Outlook or CalDAV. Scope adapter input to the current destination or implement credential-aware selection throughout."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts",
      "line": 151,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Restore the organization slug condition when billing is disabled",
      "body": "This reverses the existing condition for assigning an organization's slug. With team billing disabled, newly created organizations now receive no slug despite registering or requesting their subdomain, breaking resolution at that address. With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately alongside requestedSlug rather than being deferred. Preserve the original !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for slug."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 370,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Reuse one Google Meet conference across collective host events",
      "body": "For a collective Google Meet booking, each host's calendar receives the same event containing a conferenceData.createRequest. Each Google events.insert creates a conference for its own event, and this loop never copies the first result's conference data into subsequent inserts. The cohost's directly created calendar event therefore has a different meeting link from the main host's event. Generate the conference once and reuse its returned conference data for the other hosts."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 170,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Preserve credential IDs on video booking references",
      "body": "The new conditional always writes undefined as the credentialId for video results, discarding result.credentialId that was previously preserved. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference contains a credentialId. Newly created Zoom or other dedicated-video bookings therefore cannot delete their external meetings when cancelled."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts",
      "line": 1078,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Retain cohost destinations when the organizer has no calendar",
      "body": "If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then discards all collected teamDestinationCalendars, even when other collective hosts have connected calendars. EventManager consequently creates no events for those hosts. Initialize an array or assign the collected destinations rather than skipping them when the main destination is absent."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts",
      "line": 175,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Rebuild collective destinations before deferred calendar creation",
      "body": "handleNewBooking collects multiple host destinations but persists only destinationCalendar[0] on the booking. This confirmation handler reconstructs an array containing only that persisted calendar, so EventManager never creates the cohosts' destination events when a collective booking requires approval. The payment webhook handlers have the same limitation. Deferred creation needs to reconstruct the booked hosts' destinations, not merely wrap the organizer's calendar."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts",
      "line": 454,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Delete every host's references when cancelling a recurring series",
      "body": "Inside the new per-reference loop, the allRemainingBookings branch ignores the calendar obtained for the current reference. It instead iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials and selects the first calendar reference from each recurring booking. For collective bookings, this repeatedly deletes the organizer's event while never deleting the cohosts' events, even though all bookings are marked cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's references and resolve the credential belonging to each reference."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts",
      "line": 208,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Use reference credential IDs when requesting a collective reschedule",
      "body": "Calendar deletion still resolves credentials by integration type from only the requesting user's credentials. With the multiple-host references introduced here, two Google references are both deleted using that user's Google account, so the cohost's deletion returns 404 and is ignored. References for providers the requester has not installed are excluded entirely. The booking is marked cancelled while cohost calendar events remain; resolve each reference by its credentialId instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 147,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Preserve Google calendar selection for destinations without credential IDs",
      "body": "EventManager explicitly retains a compatibility path for destination calendars whose credentialId is absent, choosing credentials by integration type. Such a destination can never match the numeric credentialId in this lookup, so createEvent now writes to primary regardless of its configured externalId. Previously the selected externalId was honored. Keep a destination fallback for this supported legacy path."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 256,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Restore a usable Google destination fallback for updates and deletions",
      "body": "This fallback searches for an externalId equal to externalCalendarId precisely when externalCalendarId is null, undefined, or empty. Normal destination IDs cannot match that value. A booking reference without externalCalendarId therefore sends an undefined required calendarId to Google updates, despite the event containing a valid destination. The equivalent deletion fallback searches primary instead and treats a 404 as success, potentially leaving an event on a secondary calendar. Select the applicable destination rather than comparing against the missing ID."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
      "line": 496,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "perf",
      "title": "Avoid updating nontraditional calendar integrations twice",
      "body": "The new filter includes references such as closecom_other_calendar, so the main reference loop now updates those integrations. The dedicated other_calendar loop below still updates them again. For a booking with a normal calendar and Close.com connected, every reschedule, location change, or attendee update now issues two CRM writes instead of one. Exclude these references from the main loop or remove the duplicate processing."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Guard the missing destination calendar in the Google Meet fallback
findings.body: When destinationCalendar is null or empty, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar. A booking with Google Meet selected then throws while reading .integration, instead of falling back to Cal Video as before. This can happen after disconnecting Google Calendar while retaining a Google Meet event location. Use an optional access or explicitly handle the missing destination.

findings.title: Select the current host's destination before invoking calendar adapters
findings.body: Every credential receives the complete destinationCalendar array, but Office365, Lark, and CalDAV still select its first entry. Consequently, a second Outlook host attempts to create an event in the first host's calendar using the second host's credentials; CalDAV can filter out every calendar and silently report success without creating anything. Google's organizer attendee also uses the first externalId, which is not a valid email when the main destination is Outlook or CalDAV. Scope adapter input to the current destination or implement credential-aware selection throughout.

findings.title: Restore the organization slug condition when billing is disabled
findings.body: This reverses the existing condition for assigning an organization's slug. With team billing disabled, newly created organizations now receive no slug despite registering or requesting their subdomain, breaking resolution at that address. With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately alongside requestedSlug rather than being deferred. Preserve the original !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for slug.

findings.title: Reuse one Google Meet conference across collective host events
findings.body: For a collective Google Meet booking, each host's calendar receives the same event containing a conferenceData.createRequest. Each Google events.insert creates a conference for its own event, and this loop never copies the first result's conference data into subsequent inserts. The cohost's directly created calendar event therefore has a different meeting link from the main host's event. Generate the conference once and reuse its returned conference data for the other hosts.

findings.title: Preserve credential IDs on video booking references
findings.body: The new conditional always writes undefined as the credentialId for video results, discarding result.credentialId that was previously preserved. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when the video reference contains a credentialId. Newly created Zoom or other dedicated-video bookings therefore cannot delete their external meetings when cancelled.

findings.title: Retain cohost destinations when the organizer has no calendar
findings.body: If neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then discards all collected teamDestinationCalendars, even when other collective hosts have connected calendars. EventManager consequently creates no events for those hosts. Initialize an array or assign the collected destinations rather than skipping them when the main destination is absent.

findings.title: Rebuild collective destinations before deferred calendar creation
findings.body: handleNewBooking collects multiple host destinations but persists only destinationCalendar[0] on the booking. This confirmation handler reconstructs an array containing only that persisted calendar, so EventManager never creates the cohosts' destination events when a collective booking requires approval. The payment webhook handlers have the same limitation. Deferred creation needs to reconstruct the booked hosts' destinations, not merely wrap the organizer's calendar.

findings.title: Delete every host's references when cancelling a recurring series
findings.body: Inside the new per-reference loop, the allRemainingBookings branch ignores the calendar obtained for the current reference. It instead iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials and selects the first calendar reference from each recurring booking. For collective bookings, this repeatedly deletes the organizer's event while never deleting the cohosts' events, even though all bookings are marked cancelled. Iterate each updated booking's references and resolve the credential belonging to each reference.

findings.title: Use reference credential IDs when requesting a collective reschedule
findings.body: Calendar deletion still resolves credentials by integration type from only the requesting user's credentials. With the multiple-host references introduced here, two Google references are both deleted using that user's Google account, so the cohost's deletion returns 404 and is ignored. References for providers the requester has not installed are excluded entirely. The booking is marked cancelled while cohost calendar events remain; resolve each reference by its credentialId instead.

findings.title: Preserve Google calendar selection for destinations without credential IDs
findings.body: EventManager explicitly retains a compatibility path for destination calendars whose credentialId is absent, choosing credentials by integration type. Such a destination can never match the numeric credentialId in this lookup, so createEvent now writes to primary regardless of its configured externalId. Previously the selected externalId was honored. Keep a destination fallback for this supported legacy path.

findings.title: Restore a usable Google destination fallback for updates and deletions
findings.body: This fallback searches for an externalId equal to externalCalendarId precisely when externalCalendarId is null, undefined, or empty. Normal destination IDs cannot match that value. A booking reference without externalCalendarId therefore sends an undefined required calendarId to Google updates, despite the event containing a valid destination. The equivalent deletion fallback searches primary instead and treats a 404 as success, potentially leaving an event on a secondary calendar. Select the applicable destination rather than comparing against the missing ID.

findings.title: Avoid updating nontraditional calendar integrations twice
findings.body: The new filter includes references such as closecom_other_calendar, so the main reference loop now updates those integrations. The dedicated other_calendar loop below still updates them again. For a booking with a normal calendar and Close.com connected, every reschedule, location change, or attendee update now issues two CRM writes instead of one. Exclude these references from the main loop or remove the duplicate processing.
